during the Giro stage race the bone–kidny–parathyroid hormone system is activated in order to maintain calcium and phosphate homeostasis.
during the Giro 3‐week race the strong metabolic effort acted on the bone–parathyroid–kidney system.
the strong metabolic effort during a cycling stage race acts on the bone‐kidney‐parathyroid system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of bone and mineral metabolism during a long‐term stage race.
the regulation of the bone‐kidney‐parathyroid axis and the effects of the metabolic effort on this system.
the reciprocal regulation of calcium‐ and phosphorus‐regulating hormones during a high‐energy cycling stage race.

the bone–kidny–parathyroid axes is able to maintain calcium and phosphorus balance during a 3‐week cycling stage race.
the metabolic effort in a high‐intensity stage race does not affect calcium and phosphorus metabolism.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the strong metabolic effort during the Giro 3‐week race acts on the bone‐kidney‐parathyroid system and the rise in plasma FGF23 concentration might be aimed to maintain calcium and phosphorus balance.
the bone–kidny–parathyroid regulation system is able to adapt to the metabolic demand of a three‐week stage race.

the high energy expenditure of a 3‐week cycling stage race induces a rise of the plasma FGF23 concentration and a reduction in the serum inorganic phosphorus levels, which are both aimed at preserving calcium and phosphorus balance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FGF23 is a useful marker for the assessment of the bone‐kidney‐parathyroid axis in athletes.
the FGF23‐phosphorus axis is highly regulated in response to metabolic effort.
